Corporate Overview Statutory Reports Financial Statements
NOTES FORMING PART OF THE STANDALONE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
2.14 Provisions and contingent liabilities
A contingent liability exists when there is a possible but not probable obligation, or a present obligation
that may, but probably will not, require an outflow of resources. Contingent liabilities are not recognised
but are disclosed where an inflow or outflow of economic benefits is possible. Claims against the Company
where the possibility of any outflow is remote are not disclosed. Provisions are reviewed at each balance
sheet date. Refer note 2.3 for estimates.
